bug_semantics: When fixRequestBody re-emits a body as multipart/form-data, the vulnerable serializer interpolates attacker-controlled field names and values directly into boundary-delimited multipart syntax. CR/LF and boundary text in one parsed field can therefore terminate that part and inject a new field that the upstream multipart parser sees but the proxy-side non-multipart parser and policy did not see.
flaw_origin: Public PR #896 was squash-merged as 5d9f46f72010c3512a859179ec43b54f521e7fa1, but its five-member history is reconstructable. The first member, a12a59df42507659e536ce60c04ee7f97dd5aad5, is the atomic BIC: it added the multipart branch and the unescaped template interpolation in src/handlers/fix-request-body.ts. Its immediate parent f2a9fe475d4d600587df7f5bb4e0740ffd79c798 contains only the JSON and urlencoded branches. The next substantive member, 526ae10f2d19b4f74b538aa438ab57bb6f7579e4, merely moved the same serializer out of fixRequestBody and added tests.

reasoning: The vulnerability is real and requires a non-multipart input parser, an outgoing multipart content type, fixRequestBody, and attacker control of a key or value. Under those conditions, a single proxy-visible field containing CR/LF and the chosen boundary becomes multiple upstream-visible parts because the serializer writes untrusted text as multipart framing. Decomposing PR #896 avoids misclassifying its 2025 squash aggregate: member a12a59df42507659e536ce60c04ee7f97dd5aad5 first wrote the vulnerable interpolation, while its direct parent lacks the entire multipart path and 526ae10f2d19b4f74b538aa438ab57bb6f7579e4 only relocates it. The squash integration is first released in v3.0.4 and remains in the v4 line. Parallel direct fixes c13a99c5bfb5b446a3c0a5910b740740f341dea3 and a1ac3158541d670c94699a615091f8e9101b7fe6 reject CR/LF or boundary injection and enter v3.0.7 and v4.1.1 respectively. Finally, only the atomic BIC commit object is used for AI attribution; its human author/committer and marker-free message establish NOT_AI.
